newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks close with strong bounce.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks close with strong bounce.

text.p: Argentine stocks staged a relief rally Thursday and closed at session highs, coming to terms with a likely U.S. Federal Reserve interest rate hike next Tuesday, dealers said.

"You could say the uncertainty has ended. (Fed chairman Alan) Greenspan's statements today led most investors to think a rate hike is a given, so they've put it behind them and are getting on with business," said Humberto Lopez at Wainbuch traders.
The blue-chip MerVal index jumped 2.1 percent to a seven-session high of 723.53.
Greenspan said Thursday a tight labor market was creating some inflationary pressures and the Fed's mission was to act preemptively to head off any rise in prices.

Although Wall Street slumped, the bolsa was underpinned by the U.S. long bond yield, which first pierced the psychological barrier of 7.0 percent as Greenspan spoke, but then pulled back to close at 6.96 percent.
"Argentine stocks have been trying to find their feet since Tuesday, because they were already wallowing at a five-week low where they found pretty strong technical support," another trader said.
The bolsa's all-share index rose 1.3 percent, with risers smashing decliners 48 to 10 and 12 issues closing flat.
Floor volume eased to 20 million pesos from 26 million Wednesday, while over-the-counter turnover swelled to 158.2 million from 134.6 million Wednesday.

Top main-tier performers were carmakers Ciadea and Sevel, which surged 6.3 percent and 4.6 percent, respectively, and steelmakers Acindar and Siderca, up 3.4 percent and 3.3 percent, respectively. The only MerVal loser was gas distributor Transportadora de Gas del Sur, off 0.4 percent.
